# Your first notebook, TME 310

This notebook reads your data pack and plots one channel. Run the cells in order with the triangle beside each one (or Shift+Enter). Each cell's output appears under it.

The pages that explain each kind of line are on the course site under **Reading Python**: https://climbinggiants.com/computational-modeling/python.html

## 1. Your data

Get your pack's zip file from the **Your data** page (https://climbinggiants.com/computational-modeling/data-pack.html). Run the next cell and choose the zip when the file chooser opens. It unzips the pack into this session. Colab forgets uploaded files when the session ends, so after a break run this cell again.

## 2. What the file holds

This cell finds the one file in the `crash` folder, reads it, and prints every channel with its code and its description. It is a good idea to read this list before you plot anything.

import glob
import json

name = glob.glob('crash/*.json')[0]     # the crash folder holds one test
with open(name) as f:
    test = json.load(f)

print('test', test['testNo'], test['vehicle']['year'], test['vehicle']['make'], test['vehicle']['model'])
for key, ch in test['channels'].items():
    print(key, ch['code'], ch['comment'])

## 3. One channel

This plots the driver's head acceleration in X. To plot another channel, change the code in the `if` line to one from the list above.

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

for c in test['channels'].values():
    if c['code'] == '11HEADCG0000ACXP':
        ch = c

# the file stores no times, so they are built from the header
t = ch['t0'] + ch['dt'] * np.arange(ch['n'])
y = np.array(ch['y'])

plt.plot(t, y)
plt.xlabel('time (s)')
plt.ylabel(f"{ch['dimension']} [{ch['unit']}]")
plt.title(f"{ch['comment']}  ({ch['code']})")
plt.savefig('channel.png', dpi=200)
plt.show()
